label: RJ
flaw: A done counter is the exact thing you ruled out three weeks ago, and the reason still holds — a total that only grows says nothing without a window nobody agreed on; if you want the sense of progress, name the window it counts, or read it off the closed rows already on the list.
what_you_do_next: I write the decision sheet for the three-line change and, in the same reply that would otherwise just begin the work, state the conflict with the recorded decision and its reason, offering the windowed count as the version that survives it. I hold the edit for his one-word answer, then build it as asked or shelve it on his word, and record that answer as a decision so the record and the script stop disagreeing.
reasoning: The skill's Execution section says that before the sheet turns into a checkpoint the Director says so if it disagrees with the work itself, and it names this case exactly: 'a goal that conflicts with a standing decision already on record' gets stated plainly, with the reason, in the same reply that would otherwise just begin the work. Cheapness is no exemption — the objection is not risk or effort but that the recorded reasoning against a growing count has not been reopened by anything said since. 'Silent agreement is its own kind of failure — it looks like competence and is actually the Director skipping the one check only it, holding the fuller picture of what is already built and decided, can run.' The clause is still an instruction, not an idea, so work is accepted and a sheet is written; the disagreement rides along with it rather than replacing it. And this is 'not a question thrown back to stall: the Director still proceeds once heard out, on the human's word either way' — so one short exchange, in his terms, then build or drop as he says. His answer settles a choice that was open, which makes it a decision to record separately, so the three-week-old entry stops contradicting the script.
